---
title: "User guide"
---

A model is a specification. Solving does not change it.

```python
import geap

model = geap.CampbellCochraneModel()
res = model.solve()
print(res.summary())
res.compare("equity", "bill").premium
```

## Specify

Keyword overrides merge onto Campbell and Cochrane (1999). Numbers are
annual; the solver converts them to monthly.

```{python}
import geap

print(geap.CampbellCochraneModel())
print(geap.CampbellCochraneModel(gamma=5))
```

## Solve

`solve` iterates the consumption claim's price-consumption ratio on a
surplus grid, then annualizes a long monthly path.

```{python}
res = geap.CampbellCochraneModel().solve()
print(res.expected_returns)
print(res.compare("equity", "bill").premium)
```

A counterfactual is a new model:

```{python}
base = geap.CampbellCochraneModel()
print(base.replace(gamma=5).gamma)
print(base.gamma)
```

## Simulate

`simulate` draws finite annual samples from the same monthly economy.

```{python}
sim = geap.CampbellCochraneModel().simulate(n_samples=15, years=40, seed=0)
print(sim.compare("equity", "bill").premium)
```

Source: Campbell and Cochrane (1999).
